**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Do not report `"default": 0` as a missing world in `list` output.**

`list` adds a `"default"` entry before it counts quads. This happens even when the assembled EDB has no default-graph assertions. A world with zero assertions is then reported, but selecting that world fails at Line 220 with "empty or absent". The `named_graphs()` loop has the same effect for declared but empty graphs. Consumers of the listing cannot tell selectable worlds from empty ones. Report only worlds whose count is nonzero. As an alternative, flag the empty entries explicitly.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-        let mut worlds = BTreeMap::from([("default".to_owned(), 0_usize)]);
+        let mut worlds = BTreeMap::<String, usize>::new();
```
</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
    if operation == "list" {
        let mut worlds = BTreeMap::<String, usize>::new();
        for graph in edb.named_graphs() {
            let name = match edb.resolve(graph) {
                TermRef::Iri(iri) => iri.to_owned(),
                other => format!("{other:?}"),
            };
            worlds.insert(name, 0);
        }
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Review comment at @crates/pipeline/examples/recorded-class-consistency.rs around
lines 191 - 199:
Update the `list` operation’s `worlds` construction to include only worlds with
nonzero assertion counts; avoid pre-populating `"default"` or retaining
zero-count entries from `edb.named_graphs()`. Preserve the existing listing
format for selectable worlds.

After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local

```
